title: A niacinamide and bioceramide skincare regimen tested in Black women with post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (registered trial, results not out)
headline: A 60-person Brazilian trial of a full cleanser, moisturizer, 5% niacinamide serum and SPF 30 routine in Black women with facial PIH is registered with a planned end date of 31 Oct 2026; there are no results yet, no control group in the registry record, and the sponsor collaborator is a cosmetics company.
evidenceTier: Trial registry record only (ClinicalTrials.gov); no results, no publication
fit: Pigment-prone skin: Strong on population fit (Fitzpatrick IV to VI, self-identified Black women). Strong on the question, weak on evidence until results appear.
displaces: It would overlap the existing niacinamide and ceramide steps rather than add one; the useful comparison is against a simpler routine, which this design does not include.
regions: Products in the study are cosmetic; brand and availability not stated in the record
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
buzzCheck: Not applicable until a product is named; the record does not identify the brand.
summaryPoints: Observation (registry record read in full): interventional, not applicable phase, 60 women aged 18 to 55, Fitzpatrick IV to VI, self-identified Black, with facial post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. Single site, Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein, Sao Paulo. Started 19 Mar 2026; primary completion 31 Oct 2026.

Observation: the regimen is a 0.2% bioceramide cleanser, a 2% niacinamide + 1% bioceramide moisturizer, a 5% niacinamide + 3% bioceramide serum, and SPF 30 sunscreen, for 12 weeks, with visits at baseline, week 6 and week 12.

Observation: primary outcomes are HASI (an adapted MASI), investigator global assessment and standardised photography analysed in ImageJ; secondary outcomes are MelasQoL and DLQI. The record names no comparison group.
Observation: collaborator is a cosmetics company (COTY Brasil). Participants are hospital staff and students, which can bias reporting.
Inference: with no control arm, any improvement would mix the ingredients, daily sunscreen use, and a stricter routine. The record cannot separate them.
toneData: Fitzpatrick IV to VI, self-identified Black women (one of the few registered trials built around this group)
fitLine: Right population and a realistic whole-routine design, but nothing to act on until results appear; the sunscreen and routine consistency may account for much of any change.
timeline: 12-week treatment; results expected after 31 Oct 2026 completion, publication date unknown

fitAxes.why: Ceramide-containing cleanser and moisturizer are part of the tested routine, but barrier function is not a listed outcome.
Topical treatments were excluded for 1 month and depigmenting agents for 3 months before entry; use alongside a retinoid is untested.
Includes SPF 30 daily, which matters for pigment regardless of the other products.

dossier.whatItIs: A registered, single-arm-looking evaluation of a branded dermocosmetic routine rather than a single ingredient. It matters more for who was enrolled than for what was tested.

steps: Applied: 2% to 5% niacinamide with 1% to 3% bioceramides in a leave-on routine plus daily SPF 30 for 12 weeks.
Stated in the broader literature (not in this record): niacinamide can reduce melanosome transfer from melanocytes to keratinocytes; ceramides support the barrier.
Inferred: a stronger barrier and daily sun protection could reduce further darkening, but the record states no mechanism and no measurement of it.
mechanism.inferenceFlag: The mechanism lines come from general knowledge of niacinamide, not from this record, and none are being measured in this trial.
mechanism.diagramCaption: Routine (niacinamide + bioceramides + SPF 30) -> (hypothesis) less melanosome transfer and fewer new insults -> (measured) HASI, global assessment, photo analysis, quality-of-life scores.

flow.label: Cleanser, moisturizer, serum, SPF 30 for 12 weeks
flow.note: Whole routine, not a single ingredient.

flow.label: Possible effect on melanosome transfer and barrier

studies.cite: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07618572. Study on the Functional Impact of Cosmetics on Improving Self-Esteem and Quality of Life in Black Women. Sponsor: Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein; collaborator: COTY Brasil.
studies.readDepth: Registry record read in full; no results or paper exist yet
studies.design: Interventional, N/A phase, single site, planned n=60, 12 weeks; no comparator listed.
studies.who: Women 18 to 55, Fitzpatrick IV to VI, self-identified Black or brown (preta/parda), facial PIH; excluded pregnancy, type 1 diabetes, atopy, skin cancer history, recent topical or systemic treatment, corticosteroids, and PHQ-9 or GAD-7 scores of 5 or more.
results: No results posted. Status: recruiting; primary completion 31 Oct 2026.
studies.conflict: Collaborator: COTY Brasil (a cosmetics company). Funding terms not stated in the record.
studies.limits: Registry record only; protocol could change; no control arm; participants recruited from hospital staff; the exclusion of anyone with a PHQ-9 or GAD-7 score of 5 or more narrows who the quality-of-life results describe.

howToUse: Nothing to adopt. If results appear, the questions to ask are: was there a control, did sunscreen use change, and what happened at week 12 versus week 6.

expect.what: Results could be posted on the registry or published; timing is unknown.

wouldChangeVerdict: Posted results with a comparator or at least a sunscreen-only run-in
A named product with a verifiable ingredient list
Independent replication outside a cosmetics-company collaboration
dossier.transfer: Does it transfer to you? The population is the closest match I have found this year: Fitzpatrick IV to VI, self-identified Black women with PIH. That is a point in its favour. But the trial is a whole-routine test without a comparison arm in the record, so even a positive result will not isolate niacinamide, and Brazilian climate, sun exposure and sun-protection habits differ from Toronto's seasons.
